rebuttal_response: The rebuttal correctly identifies an incompatibility, but its proposed resolution rewrites Criterion 4 rather than satisfying it. The governing criterion explicitly requires P02S to own all TOML/JSON/YAML edits and permits no other prompt to own structured-file transformation units. The unchanged artifact instead assigns live YAML application and CI workflow ownership to P09 while P02S forbids live structured-file edits. Spec intent cannot override the supplied acceptance standard, so P00A-B02 remains a blocker.

findings.title: Structured-file edits remain owned and executed outside P02S
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 4: “P02S owns all structured file edits” and “no other prompt owns structured-file transformation units.”
findings.trigger: P09 updates a CI workflow YAML file, or another downstream prompt applies a live TOML/JSON/YAML transformation.
findings.consequence: A prompt other than P02S owns the live structured mutation, so the required exclusive P02S responsibility cannot be established.
findings.evidence: P02S prompt line 55 says, “Do not edit live TOML/JSON/YAML files; downstream owners apply” the codemod. P09 line 61 applies the P02S YAML codemod and the manifest assigns P09 `ci_workflow_updates`. Adding `structured_file_transformations_all_formats` to P02S does not remove that conflicting ownership.

findings.title: The existing v1 manifest was replaced instead of preserving a new version
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 7: “Confirm no existing artifacts overwritten with new versions” and the requirement that prior artifacts remain unchanged.
findings.trigger: An operator attempts to verify the manifest evidence used in earlier QA rounds.
findings.consequence: The original v1 manifest is unavailable under its original identity, preventing byte-for-byte verification and breaking artifact lineage.
findings.evidence: Checkpoint v3 describes corrections made within `prompt_manifest.resolved.v1.yaml`, says the v2 manifest was removed, and nevertheless describes the original v1 as the Round 1 artifact. The active v1 now has changed paths, statuses, timestamp, and ownership rather than preserving those corrections as a later version.

observations: The reviewed checkpoint has the same SHA-256 as round 3; no artifact repair was made this round.
P00A-B01 remains resolved: the active manifest contains 13 completed/active prompt entries with existing paths.
Current working-tree changes remain confined to the authorized P00A planning directories.
reasoning: The disk history exactly matches my three remembered verdicts. Because the artifact is unchanged, I rechecked the decisive manifest and prompt statements and adjudicated the new rebuttal against the criterion as written. The rebuttal proposes changing the acceptance criterion, which is outside this review. Both round-3 blockers therefore survive.
